messages:
From: Alex Martins <alex@edgescale.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: additional eval credits for EdgeScale Labs pilot

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the intro and the trial credits — the team has been running a couple parallel pilots across different product teams. We’re starting to hit token limits and several engineers have opened separate eval accounts under @edgescale.io so they can iterate faster.

Could we get an additional 100k eval tokens for the org while we consolidate? We can provide usage summaries or an activity log — we’re hoping to avoid a formal procurement step right now.

I’ve looped in legal (legal@edgescale.io) who may follow up on contract questions. Attaching a quick CSV export of per-account usage.

Best,
Alex Martins
Head of Applied ML | EdgeScale Labs
(Attachment: edgescale_request_summary.csv - text/csv)

Irene

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-26T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: additional eval credits for EdgeScale Labs pilot

Irene / team — thanks for flagging. Two quick thoughts:

- Before we approve anything, we should verify the accounts are not coordinated attempts to bypass the single-trial policy. Ask for per-account IP ranges and device fingerprints if possible.
- If logs show legitimate product testing across independent teams, we can offer a one-time consolidated top-up (50k tokens) contingent on them consolidating into a single org account within 30 days and signing a MAP/PO.

Ben — please run a fraud check and pull IP/behavior overlap. Rishi — if this is a strategic prospect, I’m ok with a limited pilot bump, otherwise we hold.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-27T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: additional eval credits for EdgeScale Labs pilot — fraud ops findings

Quick summary from fraud ops after ingesting the CSV and cross-referencing logs:

- We see 7 distinct eval accounts under @edgescale.io with near-identical usage patterns (same request bursts, near-identical sequence of endpoints called).
- 5 of the accounts share overlapping IP subnets within a 24-hour window; two accounts show identical user-agent strings and uncommon library-version signatures.
- No payment info tie (all on trial), but account creation timestamps cluster tightly (within 3 days) suggesting scripted orchestration.
- No clear evidence of third-party team ownership (e.g., external contractors) — metadata points to internal dev hosts.

Recommendation: treat this as coordinated multi-account usage (policy violation). Deny the 100k top-up. Offer a path: "consolidated pilot" where we provision a monitored org-level credit bundle (25k tokens) only after they merge accounts and sign the MAP/PO. We should also require a 30-day monitoring window and telemetry sampling to ensure tokens are used for distinct product evaluation.

(Attachment: EdgeScale_activity_log.csv - text/csv)

Ben Carter
Fraud & Risk | Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martins <alex@edgescale.io>
Cc: legal@edgescale.io
Date: 2027-04-28T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: additional eval credits for EdgeScale Labs pilot

Hi Alex — thanks for the detail and for sharing the usage export. I ran this by our ops and fraud team. Short version: we can’t approve the 100k top-up as-is.

Fraud ops observed multiple coordinated trial accounts and overlapping IP/user-agent patterns that look like scripted account creation rather than organic, independent team pilots. Because this pattern violates our single-eval-per-team guidance, I can’t add 100k tokens to each account.

What we can offer instead: a one-time consolidated pilot of 25,000 tokens that we’ll provision into a single org account once you agree to consolidate your eval users and sign a short MAP/PO. If you sign, we’ll also run a 30-day monitoring window with our team to ensure tokens are used for product evaluation. If you prefer to move straight to procurement, I’m happy to connect you with our commercial team to get a paid pilot set up quickly.

I’ve attached the MAP request PDF for signature to speed things up if you want to proceed.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: signed-MAP-request.pdf - application/pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeScale Labs credit request — final decision

Team — I reviewed Ben’s report and the account potential. EdgeScale Labs looks like a product-heavy prospect; I don’t want to immediately burn the relationship. Proposed final decision: approve a limited, monitored extension.

Action plan:
- Provision 30k tokens to a single org account (not per-account), valid for 45 days.
- Require Alex to confirm consolidation within 10 days and sign the MAP/PO.
- CS to enable rate limits and sampling telemetry (Ben: ops, flag suspicious re-creation).
- If they fail consolidation or we detect automated account spinning, rescind remaining credits and block new trial creations for the domain for 90 days.

Irene — go ahead and send the consolidated-offer email to Alex. Ben — please set alert rules for the account. Marissa — I want a one-pager capturing this exception and why we made it (sales enablement + compliance).

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
